title: EC2 Auto Scaling
description: Learn how Auto Scaling groups, scaling policies, health checks, and placement groups work together.

data.text: Demand for applications changes throughout the day. Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances to maintain performance and minimize costs. When traffic is high, it adds instances. When traffic drops, it removes them. This is the elastic part of EC2 in action.

An Auto Scaling group (ASG) is a collection of EC2 instances managed as a logical unit. The group maintains a desired capacity by launching or terminating instances as needed. You define the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity.

data.title: Auto Scaling Capacity Settings
items: Minimum Capacity — The fewest instances the group should have at any time.
Maximum Capacity — The most instances the group is allowed to launch.
Desired Capacity — The ideal number of running instances.

data.text: Scaling policies define when and how Auto Scaling adjusts capacity. There are three main types: simple scaling adds a fixed number of instances, step scaling adds or removes instances in steps based on the size of the alarm breach, and target tracking scales to keep a metric at a specific target.

Auto Scaling performs two types of health checks. EC2 status checks detect hardware and software failures at the hypervisor level. ELB health checks detect application-level failures from the load balancer's perspective. If an instance fails either check, Auto Scaling replaces it automatically.

Placement groups influence how EC2 instances are placed on the underlying hardware. Cluster placement groups pack instances close together on the same hardware for low-latency communication. Spread placement groups place instances on distinct hardware for maximum availability.

A rule that tells Auto Scaling when to add or remove instances.

data.title: Create an Auto Scaling Group with AWS CLI
data.content: This example creates a launch template and an Auto Scaling group with min 2, max 5 instances.
data.code:
# Create a launch template
aws ec2 create-launch-template \
  --launch-template-name my-template \
  --version-description "Version 1" \
  --launch-template-data '{
    "ImageId": "ami-0abcdef1234567890",
    "InstanceType": "t3.micro",
    "KeyName": "my-key-pair",
    "SecurityGroupIds": ["sg-12345678"]
  }'

# Create Auto Scaling group
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group \
  --auto-scaling-group-name my-asg \
  --launch-template "LaunchTemplateName=my-template" \
  --min-size 2 \
  --max-size 5 \
  --desired-capacity 2 \
  --availability-zones us-east-1a us-east-1b

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Auto Scaling automatically adjusts instance count based on demand
ASGs maintain minimum, maximum, and desired capacity
Scaling policies define when to add or remove instances
Health checks detect and replace unhealthy instances
Placement groups influence instance placement for latency or availability
